evidence.quote: | true, days when days > 0 && days <= 365 -> Ok(Some(NetEndOfMonth days))

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The due-date rule for end-of-month terms is in Tier 1 (Summa.Ledger Invoicing.dueDate). The wording is in Tier 1 (Documents.termsText and the audit trail's termsWords). Parsing and validating the form input is in the Tier 2 engine, and the storage codec is in Tier 2 (Summa.Storage). The change touches no Tier 3 or Tier 4 code, so Tier 3/4 decide no domain rule.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds no effect. dueDate uses DateTime.DaysInMonth, which is a pure calendar calculation and does not read the clock. The parser and the JSON codec are pure functions over their inputs.

evidence.quote: | true, days when days > 0 && days <= 365 -> Ok(Some(NetEndOfMonth days))
| true, days when days > 0 && days <= 365 -> Ok(Some(Net days))

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Two facts are copied, and the copies currently agree. First, the wording 'Net {days} EOM' is written separately in Documents.termsText and in the audit trail's Invoicing.termsWords; the change does not define it once and share it. Second, the change duplicates the 1-to-365 day-range predicate in a second branch of the parser instead of naming it once.

evidence.quote: | true, day when day >= 1 && day <= latestDayOfNextMonth -> Ok(Some(DayOfNextMonth day))

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The due-date rule for day-of-next-month terms, the allowed upper limit (latestDayOfNextMonth) and the ordinal wording (dayOfNextMonthText) are all defined in Tier 1 (Summa.Ledger). The Tier 2 engine validates the input against the Tier 1 limit, and the Tier 2 storage codec handles serialization. No Tier 3 or Tier 4 code changes.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds no effect. DateOnly construction and AddMonths are pure, and the parser and codec are pure functions.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The new facts each have one definition that every use references. The day limit is defined once as latestDayOfNextMonth and the engine's validation uses it. The ordinal wording is defined once in dayOfNextMonthText, which both termsText and the audit trail's termsWords call. The only restatement is '(1 to 28)' inside the error message, whose exact text the requirement prescribes, and it agrees with the definition.
